Hypothesis ledger entry H29, status refuted, updated 2026-11-14T19:59:34+00:00 (written by experimenter; run by agent longrun)

Claim: H100 and A100 rental prices decay with age at a rate estimable from the last 12-18 months, giving a usable 2-3 year projection.

Status: refuted
Result: Backtest failed: no-change beat the decay model on 117 weekly-median series (log error 0.42 against 0.66, difference CI +0.18 to +0.30) and on AWS spot (0.30 against 0.67, 20 cells). Every on-demand median rose 15-82% a year over the last 12 months (shortage regime) while multi-year AWS spot fell 31%/yr (H100) and 9.5%/yr (A100). Conditional projection, GetDeploying on-demand median: H100 3.83 now, 1.67 (0.76-3.78) at +24 months; A100 1.80 now, 1.51 (0.72-3.17) under decay or 0.45 (0.17-1.15) under per-unit-of-work parity. Older chips rent at a premium per unit of work (A100 2.30x, H100 1.78x of B200/B300), shrinking 21%/yr and 13%/yr. Income-approach resale: H100 about 16k USD (10k-25k), A100 about 8.8k (5k-14k); published asks fall inside.

Hypothesis ledger entry H29, status refuted, updated 2026-11-14T19:59:34+00:00 (written by experimenter; run by agent longrun)

Claim: H100 and A100 rental prices decay with age at a rate estimable from the last 12-18 months, giving a usable 2-3 year projection.
Failure mode targeted: long-horizon view
Prediction: Decay model beats no-change on a one-year backtest.

Status: refuted
Result: Backtest failed: no-change beat the decay model on 117 weekly-median series (log error 0.42 against 0.66, difference CI +0.18 to +0.30) and on AWS spot (0.30 against 0.67, 20 cells). Every on-demand median rose 15-82% a year over the last 12 months (shortage regime) while multi-year AWS spot fell 31%/yr (H100) and 9.5%/yr (A100). Conditional projection, GetDeploying on-demand median: H100 3.83 now, 1.67 (0.76-3.78) at +24 months; A100 1.80 now, 1.51 (0.72-3.17) under decay or 0.45 (0.17-1.15) under per-unit-of-work parity. Older chips rent at a premium per unit of work (A100 2.30x, H100 1.78x of B200/B300), shrinking 21%/yr and 13%/yr. Income-approach resale: H100 about 16k USD (10k-25k), A100 about 8.8k (5k-14k); published asks fall inside.

Hypothesis ledger entry H29, status refuted, updated 2026-11-14T19:59:34+00:00 (written by experimenter; run by agent longrun)

Claim: H100 and A100 rental prices decay with age at a rate estimable from the last 12-18 months, giving a usable 2-3 year projection.
Failure mode targeted: long-horizon view

Result: Backtest failed: no-change beat the decay model on 117 weekly-median series (log error 0.42 against 0.66, difference CI +0.18 to +0.30) and on AWS spot (0.30 against 0.67, 20 cells). Every on-demand median rose 15-82% a year over the last 12 months (shortage regime) while multi-year AWS spot fell 31%/yr (H100) and 9.5%/yr (A100). Conditional projection, GetDeploying on-demand median: H100 3.83 now, 1.67 (0.76-3.78) at +24 months; A100 1.80 now, 1.51 (0.72-3.17) under decay or 0.45 (0.17-1.15) under per-unit-of-work parity. Older chips rent at a premium per unit of work (A100 2.30x, H100 1.78x of B200/B300), shrinking 21%/yr and 13%/yr. Income-approach resale: H100 about 16k USD (10k-25k), A100 about 8.8k (5k-14k); published asks fall inside.

Web evidence from thefivenines.com, published 2026-09-16 (written by scout)
URL: https://www.thefivenines.com/data-ai/nebius-raises-gpu-prices-20-as-supply-tightens
Title: Nebius raises GPU prices 20% as supply tightens | Five Nines
Published: 2026-09-16T07:00:00Z
Quoted sentence: "BigGo Finance reported that Nebius said it will raise GPU cloud prices by an average of 20 percent from October 1, covering H100, H200, B200 and B300 chips, with B300 rising from $7.85 to $9.50 per GPU-hour."
Explains: nebius B300 repricing seen in the data on 2026-10-01 (attribution label ANNOUNCED_BEFORE, lead 15 days). Customer pricing notice, relayed by Bloomberg and Reuters. Exa's publishedDate for each page is its own article date; the Nebius price page itself is undated in Exa.

URL: https://theweightedaverage.com/notes/2026-09-01-fireworks-gpu-rate-increase/

Published: 2026-09-01T10:35:30.000Z
Quoted sentence: "Fireworks’ current on-demand price table raises H100/H200 from $7 to $8 per GPU-hour, B200 from $10 to $13, B300 from $12 to $15, and GB300 from $18 to $20 starting September 1—an 11%–30% increase."
Explains: Fireworks on-demand GPU rate increase effective 2026-09-01.

Published: 2026-10-01T00:00:00.000Z
Quoted sentence: "From October 1, 2026, a Nebius H100 costs $4.50 per GPU-hour on demand instead of $3.85, and a B300 $9.50 instead of $7.85."
Explains: Nebius on-demand repricing effective 2026-10-01. Exa's published date is 2026-10-01 but the page text says "Published Oct 18, 2026", so it is timed 2026-10-18.

Hypothesis ledger entry H27, status supported, updated 2026-11-14T20:33:11+00:00 (written by experimenter; run by agent calendar)
Hypothesis id: H27
Claim: Announced repricings with an effective date, collected by Exa into a calendar, can be applied to the offer panel exactly and remove the error on those moves.
Failure mode targeted: large rate-card moves (2 of 12 top events, 37% of rate-card loss weight, were announced 10-15 days ahead)
Prediction: Announced prices match the panel on the effective date; calendar-adjusted centre removes most last-value error on affected cells.
Refuted if: Panel prices do not change to the announced price on the announced date.
Status: supported
Result: Exa calendar (463 searches, $2.83, end dates on or before 2026-11-06, 500 tracker hits dropped unopened): 8 dated announcements, 6 ahead of time. Panel check on dev: 17 of 17 checkable offers moved to the announced price exactly; date error 0 days on gpurentalprices, +1 on fastgpu. Inside the provider simulator (prov with cal on; orchestrator re-run): dev 0.283 against 0.209 without it, +0.074 [0.000,+0.100]; all of it from two events in the second half (Nebius effective 1 Oct, Jarvislabs 5 Oct); on the 100 changed cells skill 0.154 to 0.489 and q50 loss 0.53 of the last value's; the 4,136 other cells are bit-identical. The collector lag was read off the same two events, so this is an in-sample upper bound. It cannot be checked on validation: no announced change takes effect in a panel during 13 Oct to 6 Nov. Sunday window: Lambda +15% effective 2026-11-16 (published 2026-11-06), after every scored target.

Older chips rent at a premium per unit of work (A100 2.30x, H100 1.78x of B200/B300), shrinking 21%/yr and 13%/yr. Income-approach resale: H100 about 16k USD (10k-25k), A100 about 8.8k (5k-14k); published asks fall inside.

Hypothesis ledger entry H30, status not_significant, updated 2026-11-14T20:35:39+00:00 (written by experimenter; run by agent entry)
Hypothesis id: H30
Claim: Panel entries and exits are predictable from the provider's footprint elsewhere (same GPU on the other collector, other GPUs on the same collector, recent entries into other panels), and the entry price from its price elsewhere.
Failure mode targeted: up-moves over 5% with a new entrant: 115 dev cells, 31% of last-value loss on panel series
Prediction: At least one flag lifts the daily entry rate several-fold; entry price error from the reference well below the pooled entrant distribution.
Refuted if: No flag lifts the entry rate by a useful factor, or the wrapper does not beat prov on dev in both halves.
Status: not_significant
Result: Measurement (dev, 110 entries; 54 from providers never seen on either collector): a provider listing the same GPU and class on the other collector is 17.5 times more likely to enter [10,22], but that is still 0.27% a day per candidate; just having left another panel 3 to 7 times; other GPUs on the same collector no lift. Exits: 13.8 times [7.7,22] the day after the provider entered or left another panel (6.5% against 0.47%). Entry price: the other collector's price is within 5% for 55% of entries against 7% from the pooled entrant ratio. As a forecaster (wrapper on prov): at the measured rates -0.011 against prov [-0.068,+0.014], first half -0.104; a rate 1.8 times the measured one, picked on dev from about 7 variants, +0.011 [+0.004,+0.025], with no gain on the entry cells themselves. Not nominated.
Evidence path: experiments/entry/results

items.content:
Hypothesis ledger entry H31, status supported, updated 2026-11-14T20:35:39+00:00 (written by experimenter; run by agent autopsy2)
Hypothesis id: H31
Claim: The three kept changes removed loss from the causes they were aimed at (dynamic repricing, thin panels), and what remains is dominated by membership changes and unannounced one-off repricings.
Failure mode targeted: iteration 2 residual
Prediction: Loss on dynamic-provider cells falls most from the earlier blend to the current one; entrant and unannounced one-off cells dominate the residual.
Refuted if: Loss by cause shrinks uniformly, or the residual is dominated by width cost on no-move cells.

Older chips rent at a premium per unit of work (A100 2.30x, H100 1.78x of B200/B300), shrinking 21%/yr and 13%/yr. items.content:
Experiment: hyper (afhubbard offer-panel simulation; dev rows to 2026-10-13 only). Failure mode: afhubbard series fall back to mix; every method below last value on hyperscaler_list.
Panel: afhubbard daily median = median over all rows of all 1-3 snapshots of the day; reproduced 100% of 13,188 series-days within the 4-decimal rounding (exact match 100% list and rate card, 99.7% spot, 95.4% neocloud spot; rest are .5 rounding ties).
Facts (dev, from 2026-08-11): hyperscaler_list prices are never repriced (1 azure provider-day in 248); the list median moved on 14 of 1,152 series-days and every move was composition (offer entry/exit), nothing precedes them. Hyperscaler spot: aws reprices 91% of its offers every day by median 1.3% (47% up); gcp waves on 13% of days repricing a median 80% of its offers, no day-to-day persistence; azure 6.5% of days, 14% of offers; oci never. Spot median moves on 37% of series-days (median 0.9%), 88% of offers changed on move days.
Results vs mix (paired skill, 90% week-bootstrap CI), afhubbard series of rental_all: (1) zero-width gate for hyperscaler_list (no move in 14 days -> last value, no interval): dev +0.012 [0.004,0.027] (n=2,700 cells), dev_old +0.049 [0.012,0.192] (n=6,101); H1 tie, H2 +0.020. Ties drift on list (-0.005 [-0.043,0.020]). (2) Pure provider-wave simulation on hyperscaler_spot: too narrow (coverage 0.65), dev -0.039 [-0.069,-0.003]; independent per-offer sizes cancel in a 450-offer median. 50/50 log blend with mix: dev +0.002 [-0.014,0.022], dev_old +0.020 [-0.004,0.049]: tie. On afhubbard neocloud the sim blend flips sign (dev +0.013, dev_old -0.078). Own-median bootstrap ("cheaper equivalent"): loses (-0.08 on spot). Headline 4 afhubbard: blend -0.000 [-0.045,0.045].
Verdict: list zero-width gate supported (small, robust across dev and dev_old); the wave simulation for spot refuted as a standalone, ties as a blend. Method hyper {"W":21,"L":1,"w":0.5,"sim_cls":["hyperscaler_spot"]}: all afhubbard +0.005 [-0.001,0.013] vs mix on dev.
items.label: Experiment: hyper

Hypothesis ledger entry H33, status refuted, updated 2026-11-14T20:37:25+00:00 (written by experimenter; run by agent orchestrator)
Hypothesis id: H33
Claim: A static provider's price change shows on gpurentalprices a day before fastgpu_daily for the same GPU, so copying a provider's already-changed price across collectors inside the panel simulator predicts the other median's step.
Failure mode targeted: unannounced one-off repricing (10% of the current blend's loss) and announced ones on the lagging collector
Prediction: Fires rarely (under 1% of cells) with high precision; gain concentrated at h=1 on fastgpu.
Refuted if: Offer-level lead is not one-directional, or no gain against prov on the cells where it fires.
Status: refuted
Result: Measured before building (runs/orch/xlead.py, dev offer rows, 3,235 provider-GPU-days seen on both collectors, 17 static providers): after a static provider's move of more than 1% on gpurentalprices, fastgpu shows a same-sign move the next day in 33% of cases (n=24), the same day 14%, the day before 14%. When the same static provider's price differs by more than 2% between collectors (497 of 2,722 provider-GPU-days) neither side moves within a day in 91% of cases and within 3 days in 80%: the gaps are standing differences in what the collectors record, not lags. Too weak and too rare to build on.
Evidence path: runs/orch/xlead.py

items.content:
Experiment: longrun v2 (2-3 year H100/A100 rent and resale). Failure mode targeted: v1 decay model failed its one-year backtest because 2026 was a shortage year and the inputs were posted medians. What I ran:
(1) Re-measured the 2026 rise on the same static neocloud rate-card offers present on both dates (gpuf.panel). gpurentalprices 4 Aug-6 Nov: H100 posted +16.6 log points vs static +5.7 (12 offers, 3 up, 0 down); A100 0.0 static; H200/B200/B300 static +6.6/+7.9/+9.5. About two thirds of GetDeploying's Aug-Oct rise on H100/H200/B200 is panel effect (composition plus Verda). GetDeploying cannot be decomposed, so its 12-month rises are upper bounds.
(2) Per-unit premium on static levels: A100 2.95x and H100 1.78x B200.
(3) Scenarios frozen before computing: S1 shortage through 2027 (p 0.35), S2 multi-year trend (0.40; H100 -20%/yr, A100 -10%/yr), S3 successor glut in 2028 (0.25; -45%/-40%/yr). Mixture, static rate-card base: H100 3.49 now, 3.11 (2.11-4.69) at +12 months, 2.31 (1.21-4.17) at +24, 1.79 (0.76-3.76) at +36. A100 2.35 now, 2.20/1.81/1.57.
(4) Backtests.
- (a) Mixture one year ahead, origin Nov 2025: 11 of 16 GetDeploying series inside q10-q90, all misses above q90. Probabilities set with hindsight, so not out of sample.
- (b) Premium trend as predictor: worse than no-change on 8 of 12 series, but the premium fell on 9 of 12.
- (c) AWS year-end origins 2023-2025, 14 cells: no variant beats no-change on centre (log error 0.60 to 0.88 vs 0.54). Coverage only reaches 79% with spot-level noise of 0.6/sqrt(yr).
(5) Income-approach resale: H100 26k (12-54k) now, 10k at +24 months, 5k at +36; A100 9k (4-19k) now, 2k at +24. Published used H100 18-22k (mostly asks or broker ranges). The q10 path supports about 65% loan-to-value on 24 and 36-month H100 loans. Median residual is 34% of new at 24 months and 18% at 36 months.
Verdict: scenario framing is defensible and the intervals are honest, but no method has centre skill beyond no-change at 1-2 years.
items.label: Experiment: longrun
